# #770 — graph-derivation-handler counts a deduped insert as an enqueue (same defect a61b99d fixed for distill)

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-26T07:17:48Z
Updated: 2026-08-26T07:17:48Z

---

Found by the #765 review lane (correctness), 2026-08-26.

Commit a61b99d ("a dropped insert is not an enqueued job") threads `enqueueOutcome` through `MaintenanceJob` and makes `src/maintenance-sweep.ts:196-203` skip deduped rows when counting. The sibling producer at `src/graph-derivation-handler.ts:286-295` does `enqueued.push(job)` unconditionally, so `graph_derivation_enqueue_sweep` logs `enqueued: N` including dropped inserts -- the same false-health signal, one caller over.

Not a correctness bug today: `selectSourcesNeedingDerivation` (`src/graph-derivation-handler.ts:136-141`) excludes already-derived content in its WHERE clause, so under migration 047 a released key cannot re-run finished work and the graph lane cannot wedge the way distill did. It is an observability gap in a lane the 047 header itself puts in scope ("Class fix, not a distill fix: this deadlock was available to any job kind whose key can recur").

Fix shape: read `job.enqueueOutcome` before pushing, mirroring maintenance-sweep.ts:196-203.

Related: `enqueueOutcome` is optional on `MaintenanceJob` (`src/maintenance-queue.ts:108`), so a future caller that forgets to read it silently reproduces the miscount. Only two `.enqueue(` callers exist outside tests; one reads it, this one does not.

Claim state: WRITTEN for the code references (verified by the reviewer against 2fb35c4); PROPOSED for the fix.
